text: F1.7: an autokey cipher (the message or the ciphertext becomes the key) on a scrambled alphabet; 130 cells agree with the 24 known letters once plaintext autokey's chains are written out in full.
Each cell: one search on K4, then fitting scrambled copies one at a time; ten shuffles of K4 put through the same test give the null.
K4 beats all 12 copies in 7 cells, inside the stand-ins (p 0.64); three cells 0149 called fit are dead. Planted messages found only 8 of 24 and 4 of 24: a weak test, run at its power.
